c178.title: Genes and germs
c178.story: Anna's aunt Lida works at a [[biotech]] lab, and one day she invited Anna to visit. "Here we study the human [[genome]], and every [[gene]] is part of it," she said. She showed a photo of a sheep and said it was a [[clone]]. Under the [[microscope]], Anna saw a [[mutant]] fly with tiny extra wings. Then Lida showed her a [[microbe]] that makes a dangerous [[toxin]]. "This [[enzyme]] breaks the poison down, and this [[inhibitor]] stops the bug from growing," she explained. Next, Anna looked at muscle cells and learned that the protein [[actin]] helps them move. "Any [[pathogen]], like a bacterium or a [[virus]], can make people sick," Lida said. "Our team helps doctors fight dangerous diseases like [[Ebola]] and [[anthrax]]." At home, Anna told Max, "Maybe I'll become a scientist too!"

c179.title: Brain, mood and hormones
c179.story: On Tuesday, Anna went with her friend Ira to an open lecture at medical school. The professor showed a picture of a [[neuron]], one of billions in the brain. "This outer layer is the [[cortex]]," she said. She explained how each [[receptor]] catches chemicals like [[serotonin]], which affects mood. "An [[antidepressant]] can help when a person feels sad for a long time," she said. Then she talked about [[mania]], when people barely sleep, and [[paranoia]], when they trust no one. A student asked about [[amnesia]], when a person loses memories. The professor said that [[autism]] is simply a different way a brain develops and works. Hormones matter too, like [[testosterone]], [[estrogen]] and [[insulin]], which controls blood sugar. "When you are scared, [[adrenaline]] makes your heart beat fast," she added. At the end, she tapped Ira's knee, and her leg jumped: a perfect [[reflex]]!

c180.title: A week at medical school
c180.story: Anna's friend Ira told her about a busy week at medical school. On Monday, her anatomy group respectfully studied a [[cadaver]], and the teacher used a [[scalpel]]. They looked inside the [[abdomen]] and found the small [[appendix]]. Ira also saw the [[pancreas]], which makes insulin, and the huge [[aorta]]. The teacher said the digestive [[tract]] runs from the mouth to the [[anus]]. On Wednesday, Ira watched [[triage]] in the emergency room. A man with a broken leg had surgery under [[anesthesia]]. A little boy only needed a local [[anesthetic]] for his stitches. Later, a nurse showed Ira how to put in a [[catheter]]. An old patient with a nervous [[tic]] and a [[tremor]] in his hands told jokes. After the long day, Ira felt a sharp [[spasm]] in her back. Still, she called Anna happily: "Today I signed up to be an [[organ]] donor!"

c181.title: On the hospital ward
c181.story: On her first day on the hospital ward, Ira met many patients. A young man was happy because his [[tumor]] was not cancer. A brave girl was fighting [[leukemia]], and the man next to her had [[lymphoma]]. An old teacher was weak from [[anemia]], and a boy had a rare [[syndrome]]. A little girl showed Ira her [[asthma]] inhaler. A tourist had [[diarrhea]] after drinking tap water, and a painter had [[vertigo]]. At lunch, an old doctor told her stories about [[polio]] and the first [[penicillin]]. "It was the first [[antibiotic]], and it saved millions of lives," he said. He also remembered how a quick [[antidote]] saved a farmer after a snake bite. Long ago, [[cholera]] spread through the dirty water of the city. In the evening, Ira helped a family find a quiet [[hospice]] for their grandfather. She went home tired but proud of her work.

c182.title: A castle in England
c182.story: Anna and Max visited an old castle in England and climbed its stone walls. A friendly guide said that a rich [[lord]] built the castle long ago. Later, a [[baron]] lived here, then a [[duke]], and then an [[earl]] bought it. A [[squire]] owned the village nearby, and each [[yeoman]] farmed his own land. The local [[gentry]] came to big dinners, and every [[aristocrat]] danced all night. Once, a [[monarch]] visited the castle and sat on a golden [[throne]]. His [[consort]] stood beside him and smiled at the guests. Their son was too young to rule, so his uncle became [[regent]]. A loyal [[vassal]] promised to protect the boy with his life. Years later, the boy became a wise [[sovereign]]. In the gallery, Anna saw portraits of a [[tsar]] and a [[kaiser]] who once visited too. At the end, Anna posed like a queen for Max's camera.
